title: Reissue ideas for the Larkin album and a memorial album
summary: Hughes and Maxine discuss rights, Monmouth-Evergreen, and a forty-two-song memorial album Phil Schaap might help with.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Well, what a nice project it would be to -- if these can't be took out of the vault, maybe to

re-record them right now.
What's his name? Schirmer's ought to know about that, because they were -- I don't know -- International -- I don't know.

If I wasn't absolutely destitute, I would bankroll such a project myself. I assure you, it would be marvelous to hear.
You know, Monmouth-Evergreen, they put out some stuff off original records. I think if I put the tape there, they could put it out.

And I actually started back in 1969, and I've been busier since then than I was originally. Because originally, I was more or less commercial, doing the vaudeville thing. I get invited to sing along with some of our best jazz musicians in the festivals.. And it's an opportunity for me. Let's face it, there's a couple of new generations involved here too.
